title: Truthfulness and its company
hook: a man with no excuse tells the truth anyway, and a verse comes down about the company he keeps

segments.voice: Yesterday, haya', and your line: only good. Did a pause save a word or a post? Today, the virtue that refuses to hide behind an excuse. Day one thousand three hundred nine.

Ka'b ibn Malik had no excuse. The army had marched out to Tabuk, and he had simply stayed home, putting it off day after day until it was too late. When the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, came back, others lined up with reasons, and he accepted their word. Then it was Ka'b's turn. He could talk well. He knew he could win the moment. In Sahih al-Bukhari, in paraphrase, he told the Prophet instead: I had no excuse. Today: sidq, truthfulness, and what it costs.
screen: `STAYED HOME FROM TABUK.` → `OTHERS BROUGHT EXCUSES.` → `KA'B: I HAD NO EXCUSE.`

segments.voice: It cost him. Ka'b, with two others who also told the truth, was set apart. People stopped speaking to them. Ka'b says the earth, wide as it was, felt narrow. Then the Qur'an spoke about the three. Surah al-Tawbah describes them, and their repentance accepted, and then turns to everyone listening. In Pickthall's translation: "O ye who believe! Be careful of your duty to Allah, and be with the truthful." Look at that last phrase. Not only be truthful. Be with the truthful. Sidq is a virtue, and it is also a company. And Ka'b, after all of it, said, in paraphrase from Bukhari: Allah saved me only through truthfulness, and part of my repentance is to speak nothing but the truth for the rest of my life. Then the Prophet's own description, from Ibn Mas'ud, in Bukhari, in paraphrase: truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to the Garden, and a person keeps telling the truth until he becomes a siddiq, one utterly truthful. It's a path. Each true sentence is a step, and the steps add up to a name. That's why the company matters. The people around us make honesty easier or harder. A circle where everyone shades the story makes the next lie cheaper. A circle of truthful friends makes a sentence like Ka'b's easier to say. The verse doesn't stop at be truthful. It tells you whom to stand beside.
screen: `THE EARTH FELT NARROW.` · `AL-TAWBAH: BE WITH THE TRUTHFUL.` · `STEP BY STEP TO SIDDIQ.` · `THE COMPANY YOU KEEP.`

segments.voice: Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind the people you spend the most time with, in person or on a screen. One by one, ask: with this person, is it easier to tell the truth, or harder? Don't judge anyone. Just notice. Then find one person in your life who tells you the truth even when it's awkward. Hold their face for a moment. How could you spend a little more time with them this week? If you pray, you can ask to be among the truthful. The bell holds the time.
Sidq. Truthfulness: in the tongue, in the heart, and in the company you keep, step by step toward becoming a siddiq. Today's word.

Your line: with the truthful. Today, reach out to one honest friend, or give someone the plain truth where an excuse would be easier. Tomorrow, forgiveness: pardon and overlook. Day one thousand three hundred nine.

howItsDone: Islamic teaching draws on Qur'an 9:119 and the story of Ka'b ibn Malik: truthfulness is both a personal virtue and a matter of keeping truthful company.

myth: Ka'b gave the Prophet a clever excuse
he said he had no excuse, though he knew he could have argued well.
the verse says 'be with the truthful,' not only 'be truthful'
Pickthall: be careful of your duty to Allah, and be with the truthful.
truthfulness costs nothing in Ka'b's story
he was set apart, and said the wide earth felt narrow.

fork.setup: you're Ka'b. you stayed home from Tabuk with no good reason. others are offering excuses and being believed. it's your turn. what do you say?
options: give a good excuse; you speak well.
say plainly: I had no excuse.
ask to come back another day.
fork.reveal: he told the truth, was set apart for a time, and al-Tawbah later told of the three whose repentance was accepted.

original.note: Arabic: truthfulness; a siddiq is one utterly truthful.

trapdoor: what you thought: truthfulness means not lying.
what it means: true words, a true heart, and the company of truthful people, step by step toward being a siddiq.
what a scholar hears: kunu ma'a al-sadiqin in al-Tawbah 9:119 follows the verse on the three left behind (9:118), Ka'b's story in Bukhari 4418.

sources.quoted: O ye who believe! Be careful of your duty to Allah, and be with the truthful.

sources.ref: Qur'an 9:118 (the three who were left behind; the earth, vast as it was, straitened for them)
Sahih al-Bukhari 4418 (Ka'b ibn Malik: staying behind from Tabuk, no excuse, saved by truthfulness)
Sahih al-Bukhari 6094 (Ibn Mas'ud: truthfulness leads to righteousness; written as a siddiq)

notes: Ka'b's story is condensed; the length of the separation is left out deliberately. Confirm that 'two others who also told the truth' matches the report (Murara ibn al-Rabi' and Hilal ibn Umayya).
